## Soft Metadata

> [!WARNING]
> **Tier 2 (community estimate)** — Soft Metadata below adapted from T&F publisher pages and domain knowledge of clinical neuropsychology editorial culture (INS — International Neuropsychological Society). Submission practitioners are invited to upgrade individual claims to Tier 1 via `/ja-validate`. See [SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md](../../../../SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md) for the Skeleton → Tier 2 → Tier 1 lifecycle.

> **The core value of this entry.** OpenAlex cannot fill any of these — they require lived experience and community knowledge. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidance.

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | High — international clinical neuropsychology |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Low-Medium — paradigm-unified |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | High — cultural neuropsychology |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Clinical + experimental neuropsychology — TBI, stroke, dementia, neuropsychological assessment, cognitive rehabilitation, lesion-symptom mapping, experimental cognitive neuroscience with clinical implications |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (strong)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must demonstrate **clinical + experimental neuropsychology contribution** — bridges INS-affiliated clinical work and experimental cognitive neuroscience.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Pure cognitive neuroscience redirected to JoCN; pure cognitive psychology redirected to JEP family.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 5 | Core |
| Qualitative interviews | 1 | Rare |
| Autoethnography | 0 | Outside scope |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 2 | With clinical implications |
| Mixed methods | 2 | Quant-dominant |
| Meta-analysis | 5 | Welcomed |
| Neuropsychological assessment | 5 | Core method |
| Lesion-behavior studies | 5 | Distinctive strength |

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Manuscripts without clinical-experimental neuropsychology focus
- AI use without disclosure per T&F policy
- Pure cognitive neuroscience without clinical population

### Soft Tax

Low for INS clinical-experimental tradition.

### Best Suited For

- TBI / stroke / dementia neuropsychological research
- Lesion-symptom mapping studies
- Cognitive rehabilitation
- Neuropsychological assessment development
- Clinical-experimental cognitive neuroscience
- INS-community clinical neuropsychology

### Not Recommended For

- Pure cognitive neuroscience (consider JoCN)
- Pure cognitive psychology (consider JEP family)
- Pure clinical psychology without neuropsychology (consider JCCP)

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Neuropsychology](./neuropsychology.md) | APA Division 40 peer |
| 2 | [Archives of Clinical Neuropsychology](./archives-of-clinical-neuropsychology.md) | NAN-affiliated clinical neuropsychology |
| 3 | [Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience](./journal-of-cognitive-neuroscience.md) | If cognitive-mechanism focus dominates |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from JoCN as "too clinical," JCEN is the T&F INS-affiliated home.
